implementation_notes: In Rust the lock cannot be left unpaired: Mutex::lock returns a MutexGuard that owns the lock and releases it in Drop, so the critical section is the guard's lifetime and the compiler keeps early returns honest. Errors are part of the type - lock() returns LockResult because a mutex is poisoned when a thread panics while holding it - and RwLock offers read()/write() guards for reader/writer semantics. A manual unlock does not exist in the standard API; the classic alternative (an atomic for a single word, channels or an actor for ownership transfer) is chosen when sharing is not the right model at all.
pitfalls: A std guard must not be held across .await: the future then fails the Send bound at compile time (or you block the executor); async code needs an async-aware mutex.
Poisoning turns a panicked holder into an error for every later locker; decide explicitly whether to propagate, recover with into_inner, or clear_poison.
std::sync::Mutex is not reentrant: locking it twice on one thread deadlocks, and lock-order bugs between several guards are invisible to the compiler.

variants.name: async locks held across await (tokio::sync::Mutex)
variants.implementation_notes: When the critical section must await, the guard has to come from an async-aware lock: tokio::sync::Mutex::lock().await returns a guard that may be held across await points and is Send, so the compile-time restriction of the std variant disappears and waiting tasks yield instead of blocking a thread. It does not poison after a panic, so a panicking task can leave the protected data inconsistent and there is no LockResult to signal it. Prefer message passing or a dedicated actor task when the operation is request/reply rather than genuinely shared mutation.
pitfalls: Holding a tokio guard across a long await serializes every task that needs the mutex; scope the guard tightly or clone the data out before awaiting.
tokio::sync::Mutex is more expensive than the std one: use it only where the guard must cross an await, not as a default replacement.
No poisoning: a panic in the middle of an update leaves state that other tasks will observe as valid.
